The Paris Agreement aims to hold “the in­crease in the global av­er­age temperature to well be­low 2 °C above pre-in­dus­tri­al levels”.

Assuming that global climate policies stay the way they are today, and no additional measures are taken to tackle climate change:
1.   What is your expectation for the global av­er­age temperature rise by the end of this century under these conditions?
2.   On a scale from 1 (not at all confident) to 5 (very confident), how confident are you about your assessment in the previous question?
3.   Please indicate to what extent you agree with the following statements.
Climate change represents a sig­nif­i­cant issue for economies and financial markets.
With the right measures, it is possible to achieve a climate-neu­tral econ­o­my by 2050.
The econ­o­my can become climate-neu­tral while growing at the same time.
As long as there is no suitable replacement tech­nol­o­gy, in­vest­ment should still flow into emissions-intensive industries.
Responding to climate change requires that emissions-intensive companies have the funding to transition to low-emission technologies.
Responding to climate change requires shrinking emissions-intensive industries and growing low-emissions industries.
Technological innovation will be the decisive determinant of achieving a climate-neu­tral econ­o­my.
